decision: a port takes an agreement only from a bridge that names the port's own root, where 802.1D-2004 takes any from a root, alternate or backup port that is no better than what the port holds
why: the gate's property test failed once, at fast-check's seed 415198600: a bridge with a cable from one of its ports to another lost the root, and an agreement that the far port had sent as a backup reached the near one after it had become designated for the old root, so both ends forwarded until the next message. A bridge that answers a proposal has read it, so it has the proposer's root: the rule refuses no answer that is one
evidence: .audit/phase2/spanning-tree/results/moments.txt: of 160,000 random wirings of five bridges a loop carried at some moment in 587 at 8f50630 and in 103 with the rule; src/runtime/rstp.test.ts a port takes no answer that is to what it said of another root; red: a port takes an agreement whatever root it names

decision: known limit: a loop can carry for an instant while the tree changes, and a frame that is on a cable in that instant can come back to a switch once. The property test of any wiring now asks that no loop is left when the bridges are at rest, where it had asked that none carry at any moment
why: of the 103 moments that are left, the one that was traced was an answer to what a port had said of the same root at another cost. To refuse those an answer would have to say which proposal it is to, and a BPDU has no field for that. In none of 160,000 wirings was a loop left at rest. On the fabric, with a broadcast from every machine in the instant of each change to a cable, a frame came round after 22,375 of 1,130,999 changes, and no storm was still on 150 ms later. The fabric begins a storm with the first such frame, so the lab can report a storm of one frame with spanning tree on
evidence: .audit/phase2/spanning-tree/results/moments.txt; .audit/phase2/spanning-tree/results/fuzz.txt, with busy; with no traffic in the instant of a change no frame looped in 40,000 more labs
result: known limit, to tell the user. That real switches do the same is from memory of the standard and of a paper on counting to infinity, neither read in this session
